project.name: TabuLens
project.title: Dataset Readiness and Anomaly Screening with Python
project.author: Divya Dhiman
project.institution: Indira Gandhi Delhi Technical University for Women
project.subject: AI Programming Tools (AIPT)

aim: To build a simple Python application that reads tabular data, identifies common quality problems, creates an explainable cleaned copy, visualizes the dataset, and suggests unusual numeric records for review.
problem: Small tabular datasets often reach analysis with missing values, duplicate rows, inconsistent types, or unusual records. Beginners may train a model before noticing these problems. TabuLens places a transparent readiness check before later analysis.
workflow: Read a CSV file into a Pandas DataFrame.
Profile rows, columns, types, missing values, duplicates, and constant columns.
Create a cleaned copy using duplicate removal, median filling, and mode filling.
Visualize quality issues and numeric relationships.
Use Isolation Forest to suggest unusual numeric records for human review.
Export the cleaned DataFrame as a new CSV file.
learning: Python functions, modules, packages, file paths, and file handling.
Object-oriented programming through the DatasetAnalyzer class.
Pandas and NumPy for tabular operations.
Plotly and Streamlit for interactive visualization.
Scikit-learn for preprocessing and Isolation Forest anomaly screening.
limitations: The readiness score is a transparent heuristic rather than a universal data-quality standard.
Anomaly flags indicate unusual numeric patterns, not incorrect records.
CSV parsing still depends on the encoding and delimiter supplied by the user.
Subject knowledge is required before changing or removing real observations.
